title: The report and the tender plant
summary: Isaiah’s words ask who believed the report and describe the servant growing like a tender plant and a root out of dry ground.

explicit_facts.text: The words ask who believed the report and to whom the arm of the Lord is revealed.
The servant grows before him as a tender plant and as a root out of dry ground; he has no form or comeliness, and no beauty that people should desire.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A small plant or root emerging from dry ground can illustrate the comparison.
unspecified_visual_details: The servant's appearance, age, clothing, and setting are not specified.

narration.text: Who hath believed our report, and to whom is the arm of the Lord revealed?
For he shall grow up before him as a tender plant, and as a root out of dry ground;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The plant and root are figures of speech, not a narrated visible event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a specific historical person or assert a named identity for the servant.

title: Despised and rejected
summary: The servant is described as despised, rejected, acquainted with grief, and bearing griefs and sorrows, though people esteem him stricken and afflicted.

explicit_facts.text: The servant is described as despised and rejected, a man of sorrows acquainted with grief; the speakers hid their faces and did not esteem him.
He bore griefs and carried sorrows, though people esteemed him stricken, smitten of God, and afflicted.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A restrained depiction of people turning their faces away could illustrate the stated rejection.
unspecified_visual_details: The servant's appearance, the people, and the setting are not specified.

narration.text: He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief;
Surely he has borne our griefs, and carried our sorrows;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The servant's bearing griefs and sorrows is stated; no specific visible action is narrated.
prohibited_inventions: Do not add a specific crowd, cause, or event of rejection.

title: Wounded for transgressions
summary: The passage says the servant was wounded and bruised for others’ transgressions, and compares those who strayed to sheep.

explicit_facts.text: The servant was wounded for transgressions and bruised for iniquities; his chastisement brought peace, and with his stripes people are healed.
All have gone astray like sheep and turned to their own way; the Lord laid the iniquities of all on him.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Sheep straying can illustrate the explicit comparison.
unspecified_visual_details: No particular injury, people, sheep, or location is described.

narration.text: But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities;
All we, like sheep, have gone astray;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The sheep comparison is figurative; do not depict it as a literal event involving the people.
prohibited_inventions: No graphic wounds, blood, or visible supernatural transfer of iniquities.

title: Silent before judgment
summary: The servant is described as oppressed and afflicted without speaking, brought like a lamb to slaughter, and taken from prison and judgment before being cut off from the land of the living.

explicit_facts.text: He was oppressed and afflicted, yet did not open his mouth; he is compared to a lamb brought to slaughter and a sheep silent before shearers.
He was taken from prison and judgment and cut off from the land of the living for the transgressions of the speaker's people.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A silent, restrained figure may convey the stated lack of speech.
unspecified_visual_details: The prison, judgment, people present, manner of removal, and the servant's appearance are unspecified.

narration.text: He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he opened not his mouth;
He was taken from prison and from judgment;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The lamb and sheep language is comparison, not instruction to stage a literal slaughter.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a trial, guards, accusers, or a specific execution.

title: Grave among wicked and rich
summary: The servant is said to have made his grave with the wicked and with the rich in his death, despite doing no evil and speaking no deceit.

explicit_facts.text: He made his grave with the wicked and with the rich in his death; he had done no evil and had no deceit in his mouth.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A grave may be shown without adding details about its location or construction.
unspecified_visual_details: The grave's appearance, location, and the identities of the wicked and rich are unspecified.

narration.text: And he made his grave with the wicked, and with the rich in his death;

prohibited_inventions: Do not identify companions or depict a specific burial event.

title: Offering and promised outcome
summary: The passage describes the servant's soul as an offering for sin and says he will see his seed, prolong his days, and justify many by bearing their iniquities.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord put him to grief; when his soul is made an offering for sin, he shall see his seed, prolong his days, and the Lord's pleasure shall prosper in his hand.
He shall see the travail of his soul and be satisfied; by his knowledge the righteous servant shall justify many, for he shall bear their iniquities.

unspecified_visual_details: The seed, the servant's appearance, and how the promised outcomes appear are unspecified.

narration.text: he shall see his seed, he shall prolong his days,
by his knowledge shall my righteous servant justify many;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The passage states future outcomes; it does not narrate them as present visible events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a resurrection, descendants, or a divine figure not explicitly described.

title: Intercession for transgressors
summary: The servant is promised a portion with the great and is described as poured out unto death, numbered with transgressors, bearing many’s sins, and making intercession for transgressors.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker says the servant will receive a portion with the great and divide spoil with the strong.
He poured out his soul unto death, was numbered with transgressors, bore the sins of many, and made intercession for transgressors.

unspecified_visual_details: The great, the strong, the transgressors, and the setting are unspecified.

narration.text: and he was numbered with the transgressors;
and made intercession for the transgressors.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The passage summarizes the servant's suffering and intercession; it does not establish a specific present-tense scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage a battle, spoil-taking, or specific act of intercession not narrated here.
